key_provisions: Amends Ala. Code Sections 40-9B-3, 40-9B-4, 40-9B-4.1, and 40-23-35. Limits data processing center abatement periods beginning 2027-01-01, generally to 20 years, with added 10-year extension paths for certain investments. Requires certain 100 MW-plus data processing centers to pay state noneducational ad valorem taxes and sales/use tax on specified construction, power, backup generation, and battery purchases beginning 2027-01-01, subject to targeted-county gubernatorial authority. Extends the data processing center abatement sunset.

sponsors: Representatives Rafferty, Hulsey, Tillman (engrossed bill author line; given-name identities not independently established)

status: Engrossed (passed House of Origin, Roll Call 945/946/947) 2026-03-17; no further action recorded; died at sine die 2026-04-09 without Senate floor action (companion SB270 was the vehicle enacted)
key_provisions: Engrossed proposal would add public-interest review criteria for retail electric service contracts with large-load customers, including incremental cost recovery and positive benefits to other customers. Its large-load-customer definition uses expected peak demand of 100 MW or greater at one or more contiguous parcels and is not confined to data processing centers. The text separately uses the term large load data center customer in the incremental-cost definition; that wording difference is not silently normalized.

status: Carried Over to the Call of the Chair (House, Second Reading engrossed substitute stage) 2026-04-09; died at sine die without a House floor vote (companion HB399 was the vehicle enacted)
key_provisions: Senate tax-abatement vehicle with the same core policy as HB399: shorter maximum abatement periods, state tax collection on certain large data processing center purchases, and extended incentive sunset.

sponsors: Senate author: Bell; joint sponsor: Rafferty (as listed by the Secretary of State act docket)
key_provisions: Adds Ala. Code Section 37-4-22.1. Defines a "large load data center customer" as a data processing center customer with expected total peak demand of 150 MW or greater on contiguous parcels. Directs PSC public-interest review of retail electric service contracts to consider recovery of incremental costs from the data center and positive benefits for other retail electric customers.

status: Heard and held in House Energy Committee 2026-02-03; current status (H) ENE, then CRA, status date 2026-01-20
key_provisions: Not a moratorium. Regulates "large energy use facilities" through RCA-approved utility contracts, cost-causation rules, long-term service commitments, direct assignment of facility-driven utility costs, and municipal community benefit agreements before contract approval. The introduced threshold is 20 MW peak electric demand or 20 percent of prior-year utility sales, and 2 billion standard cubic feet of gas annually or 20 percent of prior-year gas sales.

sponsors: Reps. George Rauscher, Mia Costello, Ky Holland

status: (H) FIN; status date 2025-04-11 (no further action recorded through 2026-07-31)
key_provisions: Not a moratorium. Would establish a Joint Legislative Task Force on Artificial Intelligence. The proposal is relevant because it covers AI development and policy risks, but it does not impose siting, utility, or permitting restrictions on data centers.

status: Passed Senate 2026-05-16 (Y14 N5 E1 on reconsideration) as CSSB 250(CRA); transmitted to House, read first time and referred to House Community & Regional Affairs 2026-05-17; Heard & Held (recessed to call of the chair) 2026-05-18; current status (H) CRA, status date 2026-05-17
key_provisions: Not a moratorium. Directly regulates data centers and utility service. The committee substitute requires data centers to pay facility-driven utility costs, provide financial security for utility capital investments above $1 million, use contracts that avoid fuel-supply and reliability risk shifting, include backup power and reliability planning, execute municipal CBAs, address waste heat, water use, broadband interconnection, digital equity, and file decommissioning and recycling plans. The committee substitute exempts data centers below 15 MW peak electric demand and 1.5 billion standard cubic feet of annual gas use.
